issue.title: Mobile Feature Audit [Epic]
issue.body:
## Objective

Audit the existing features in the mobile application to confirm that they are complete and working as expected.

The audit will:

- Establish a clear baseline of current functionality before implementing the new UI designs.
- Identify incomplete, broken, or undocumented behavior.
- Reduce launch risk for the ETEN Summit in November 2026.
- Produce a documented assessment and actionable development tickets for each identified gap.

## Features in Scope

Each feature should have its own sub-issue under this epic:

- Drafting page
- Play, record, and re-record audio
- Going offline
- Returning online and synchronizing changes
- Viewing and listening to resources
- Chapter assignment and claiming
- Offline chapter assignment
- Pericope view

## Audit Process

For each feature:

1. Select a feature and self-assign its corresponding sub-issue in this epic.
2. Review all related GitHub issues, including issues marked `Done`.
3. Document the expected behavior based on the related issues and the current product requirements.
4. Test the feature using the latest supported mobile build.
5. Create an assessment document under:

   ```text
   docs/assessments/<feature-name>/
   ```

6. Record:
   - The build and environment tested.
   - The device and operating-system version tested.
   - The related GitHub issues reviewed.
   - The scenarios tested.
   - The expected and actual behavior.
   - Any gaps, defects, inconsistencies, or unanswered questions.
   - Supporting evidence, such as screenshots, recordings, or logs, where useful.
   - **_When a feature uses mock data and the API blocker has been implemented, this is a gap. We should remove the mocks and ensure QA has data to test against. If the feature is using mock data and the api functionality is not in place, ensure there is a ticket for it marked as 'mobile requirement' and we will make sure that it gets worked._**

## When a Gap Is Found

For every confirmed gap:

1. Create a development task document at:

   ```text
   docs/assessments/<feature-name>/tickets/<ticket-name>.md
   ```

2. Create a corresponding GitHub issue.
3. In the issue:
   - Describe the expected and actual behavior.
   - Include clear reproduction steps and acceptance criteria.
   - Link to the assessment document.
   - Link to the related original or historical GitHub issues.
   - Apply the appropriate `dev ready` status or label.
4. Either self-assign the development work or leave it unassigned and available for another developer.
5. Commit the assessment and development task documents to the appropriate repository.
6. Link the new gap issue from the feature audit sub-issue.

Before creating a new issue, verify that an open issue does not already cover the gap. If one exists, update and link the existing issue instead.

## When No Gaps Are Found

If the feature works as expected:

1. Complete and commit the assessment document to the `fluent-mobile` repository.
2. Add a comment to the feature audit sub-issue containing:
   - A link to the merged assessment document.
   - The build, environment, devices, and operating-system versions tested.
   - A brief summary of the successful result.
3. Close the sub-issue.

## API-Related Gaps

If a gap requires API changes:

1. Document the API findings in the `fluent-api` repository.
2. Create the development task document in the appropriate API assessment directory.
3. Create or update the corresponding GitHub issue in the API repository.
4. Link the API assessment and issue from the mobile assessment.
5. Keep the mobile audit sub-issue open until the dependency is resolved or explicitly accepted as follow-up work.

## Definition of Done

A feature audit sub-issue is complete when:

- All relevant historical and current issues have been reviewed and linked.
- Expected behavior and test scenarios are documented.
- The feature has been tested on the agreed build and supported device matrix.
- Online, offline, and synchronization behavior has been tested where applicable.
- Every confirmed gap has an actionable issue with acceptance criteria.
- Mobile and API dependencies are cross-linked.
- The assessment document has been reviewed and merged.
- The audit sub-issue includes the final assessment link and result.

## Epic Completion Criteria

This epic is complete when:

- [ ] Every feature in scope has a completed sub-issue.
- [ ] Every assessment document has been merged.
- [ ] Every identified gap has been resolved or captured in a prioritized development issue.
- [ ] Any unresolved launch risks are clearly documented and assigned an owner.


[Below is a template](https://github.com/eten-tech-foundation/fluent-mobile/issues/526#issuecomment-5667759582) that can be used for each audit. Simply copy the md and let AI fill it out with the test results.
